nodes.label: CFI Trial Procedure
nodes.summary: Trial by judge and jury, pre-trial review, arraignment, prosecution/defence case, summing up, verdict, sentencing.

nodes.label: Allocation and Mode of Trial
nodes.summary: CFI trial by judge and jury for indictable offences. Pre-trial review (PTR) under Practice Direction 9.2 to narrow issues.

nodes.label: Judge and Jury
nodes.summary: Judge rules on law, sums up, directs jury; jury decides facts. Jury selection under Jury Ordinance (Cap 3) s.4; challenges for cause or peremptory. Discharge of juror if unable to understand proceedings (s.4(2)).

nodes.label: Jury Ordinance (Cap 3) s.4
nodes.summary: Jury selection and discharge of juror.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Chan Hon Wing (2006)
nodes.summary: Discharge of juror unable to understand proceedings.

nodes.label: Arraignment and Plea
nodes.summary: Accused arraigned before jury; plea taken from each count.

nodes.label: Prosecution Opening and Case
nodes.summary: Opening address; then evidence led. Voir dire: challenges to admissibility of evidence (confessions, identification, etc.) heard in absence of jury.

nodes.label: No Case to Answer Submission
nodes.summary: At close of prosecution case, accused may submit no case. Test: could a reasonable jury properly directed convict on the evidence? (Galbraith test). HK application: judge must not usurp jury function.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Wong Sau Ming (2003) 6 HKCFAR 163
nodes.summary: Galbraith test applied in HK for no-case submissions.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Lee Kwok Wah (2008) 11 HKCFAR 318
nodes.summary: Judge must not usurp jury function in no-case submission.

nodes.label: Defence Case
nodes.summary: Defence opening (optional), then evidence. Accused may testify or remain silent; silence cannot be used to strengthen prosecution case but may be subject to inference in limited circumstances (Cap 8 s.54).

nodes.label: Evidence Ordinance (Cap 8) s.54
nodes.summary: Accused's silence: cannot strengthen prosecution case but inference may be drawn in limited circumstances.

nodes.label: Witnesses and Evidence
nodes.summary: Competence and compellability. Expert evidence: governed by common law admissibility rules; expert must give objective opinion. Vulnerable witnesses: special procedures under Cap 221 Part IIIA.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) Part IIIA
nodes.summary: Special procedures for vulnerable witnesses.

nodes.label: Evidence From Outside Hong Kong by Live TV Link
nodes.summary: Cap 221 Part IIIB: witness abroad may give evidence by live television link if court satisfied it is in the interests of justice and technical arrangements satisfactory.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) Part IIIB (s.79I)
nodes.summary: Evidence from outside Hong Kong by live television link.

nodes.label: Summing Up and Jury Directions
nodes.summary: Judge must sum up facts and law; direct on burden and standard of proof. Lucas direction for lies (*R v Lucas* (1981)). Circumstantial evidence direction: inference of guilt must be only rational inference. Turnbull guidelines for identification. Good character direction: credibility and propensity.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Amarjit
nodes.summary: Circumstantial evidence, lies/flight directions.

nodes.label: Verdict
nodes.summary: Unanimous verdict preferred; majority verdict possible after time and under Cap 3 s.24 (at least 7:2 or 6:1 in 9/7-person jury). Jury to be discharged if unable to agree; retrial possible.

nodes.label: Jury Ordinance (Cap 3) s.24
nodes.summary: Majority verdict: at least 7:2 or 6:1 in 9/7-person jury.

nodes.label: Sentencing After Verdict
nodes.summary: After conviction, sentencing adjourned for reports if necessary. Mitigation; victim impact statement.

nodes.label: CFI Trial Flow: Allocation
nodes.summary: Step 1: Allocation to CFI; pre-trial review to narrow issues.

nodes.label: CFI Trial Flow: Judge and Jury Empaneled
nodes.summary: Step 2: Judge assigned; jury selected and sworn.

nodes.label: CFI Trial Flow: Arraignment
nodes.summary: Step 3: Accused arraigned; plea taken before jury.

nodes.label: CFI Trial Flow: Prosecution Case
nodes.summary: Step 4: Prosecution opening; evidence led; voir dire if needed.

nodes.label: CFI Trial Flow: No Case Submission
nodes.summary: Step 5: Defence may submit no case to answer at close of prosecution case.

nodes.label: CFI Trial Flow: Defence Case
nodes.summary: Step 6: Defence opening (optional); defence evidence led.

nodes.label: CFI Trial Flow: Summing Up
nodes.summary: Step 7: Judge sums up facts and law; directs jury on burden, standard, and specific issues.

nodes.label: CFI Trial Flow: Verdict and Sentencing
nodes.summary: Step 8: Jury returns verdict; if guilty, sentencing hearing (may be adjourned for reports).
